bull_bear.body: Reinvestment in talent acquisition, digital capabilities (BIM/AI), and international business development; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on organic growth via empanelments and JV partnerships
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Dependence on government payments (though 100% guaranteed); slow international project conversion cycles (2-year lead time); bid win rate currently low at 1% abroad (targeting 5-10%); potential delays in land acquisition affecting certification and cash flow
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, proactive, and strategically focused; management emphasizes recovery from debarment, sectoral diversification, and digital transformation; tone is optimistic on Q3/Q4 performance and international pipeline
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite 90% order book from NHAI, management is actively reducing dependency by targeting state governments with higher margins; international revenue potential is underappreciated — Mozambique project already delivered, with Ghana/Zambia in advanced talks; BIM/AI adoption is not just efficiency play but a competitive moat for winning larger global tenders
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Over two decades of infrastructure-consultancy experience with 200+ completed projects across 23 states and 25+ government clients
- Multidisciplinary capability spanning roads and highways, expressways, bridges, tunnels, railways, metro, airports, buildings, ports, PHE and urban infrastructure
- End-to-end service ladder from feasibility and DPR through design, PMC, construction supervision, O&M and asset management, allowing participation at several stages of one project
- Deep technical bench - a team of 400+ engineers and infrastructure professionals, with 88 new regular hires and 36 consultant engagements added during FY 2025-26
- Track record on nationally significant assignments including the Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, the Delhi-Vadodara section of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway and the Savitri River Bridge
- Long-standing relationships with government authorities and institutional clients built over more than two decades of delivery
- Demonstrated ability to execute to international standards - first World Bank-funded assignment completed in Mozambique
- Healthy order book and positive project-level profitability across most ongoing assignments despite the FY 2025-26 accounting-estimate revisions
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on government and institutional infrastructure spending and the pace of project awards — The business is substantially dependent on the pace of infrastructure development, project awards, government and institutional spending and timely execution; any slowdown in infrastructure investment, delays in project awards or changes in government priorities may impact order inflows and business performance. The MD&A separately flags that National Highway project awarding has moderated on land-acquisition and execution delays.
- Competitive bidding and margin pressure — Assignments are won through competitive tenders; increased competition, pricing pressure and changes in tender conditions may affect the ability to secure new work and exert pressure on project margins. The Company says it evaluates opportunities on technical suitability, commercial viability, execution requirements and risk-return profile.
- Project execution risk outside the Company's control — Infrastructure projects may be delayed by statutory approvals, land acquisition, scope changes, client-related dependencies and other circumstances beyond the Company's direct control, affecting project timelines, billing and collections.
- Receivables, certification and working-capital risk — Financial performance is influenced by the timing of project awards, execution and receipt of payments from clients; delays in certification or collection of receivables may affect working capital and cash flows. Improving cash flows and working capital is one of management's stated priorities for the coming year.
- Availability and retention of qualified technical personnel — Consultancy and project management are knowledge-intensive; the ability to execute depends on availability of experienced engineers, technical professionals and project-management personnel, making attrition and hiring a structural constraint on growth.
- Regulatory and contractual risk — Changes in applicable laws, regulations, contractual requirements or government policies may affect project execution and compliance obligations towards clients and regulatory authorities.
- Execution risk in new segments and new markets — Expansion into Wayside Amenities, allied infrastructure and international markets brings new execution requirements and competitive challenges, and overseas assignments carry jurisdiction-specific regulatory, contractual, commercial and geopolitical considerations. Management says such opportunities will be pursued in a calibrated manner.
- Estimate and revenue-recognition risk on long-duration contracts — FY 2025-26 results were materially reduced by revisions to project cost and margin estimates under Ind AS 8 and Ind AS 115 following a detailed review of select long-term contracts - demonstrating that percentage-of-completion estimates on multi-year mandates can swing reported revenue and profit sharply even without a cash impact.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Revenue mix: 80% PMC (incl. O&M & construction supervision), 20% DPR; O&M: 40% of revenue; Construction supervision: 40%; DPR: 20%; New verticals: aviation (MIHAN INR1.63cr), traffic census (PWD empanelment), railways (3 projects), metros (4 MMRDA projects)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body: Dhruv Consultancy Services Limited plans, designs, supervises and advises on transportation and urban infrastructure projects for government and institutional clients in India and abroad. Its end-to-end services cover feasibility studies, DPR preparation, design and engineering, project management, construction supervision, O&M, asset management and technical advisory. Infrastructure consultancy remains the core of the business, with marquee assignments including the Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, the Delhi-Vadodara section of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, the Narnaul Bypass and NH-11 and the Savitri River Bridge.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Infrastructure consultancy:** Feasibility studies, Detailed Project Reports (DPR), Design and engineering, Construction supervision, Operation & maintenance consultancy, Asset management, Technical advisory
- **Project management consultancy:** Project management consultancy (PMC), Authority Engineer / Independent Engineer services, Lenders' Independent Engineer (LIE) and similar technical advisory (capability being built)
- **Wayside Amenities:** Verul Wayside Amenity project near the Ellora Caves
- **Airport infrastructure:** Runway and taxiway planning, Landside connectivity and utility infrastructure, Terminal-area development and associated transportation networks
business.title: Products & brands

business.body: - Dhruv International Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in the United Kingdom, shown in Form AOC-1 Part A with acquisition date 9th February 2024, financial year ending March 31, 2026 and reporting currency British pound sterling. The subsidiary is yet to commence its operations.

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin compressed in H1 due to debarment and lower certification delays; targeting 30-35% in new sectors (aviation, metros); cost control maintained via low attrition (3-4%) and in-house talent pool; USD-denominated international contracts improve margin resilience
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Q3/Q4 to outperform H1; Margin: targeting 30-35% in new sectors (aviation, metros); Order inflow: INR70-80cr expected by end of Q4FY26 from current INR250cr bid pipeline; Capex/Commissioning: none planned; digital tools implementation ongoing
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR200 crores unexecuted, to be executed over 2.5-3 years; 90% from NHAI/MoRTH, rest from MSIDC, CIDCO, MADC, OBCC
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: International expansion in Africa (Ghana, Zambia, Tanzania, Cambodia) and Southeast Asia; potential for large-ticket airport projects (INR10-15cr each); state government projects (INR25cr+ ticket size); BIM/AI adoption enabling higher project throughput
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the core roads-and-highways consultancy business by improving project execution, expanding client relationships and enhancing engineering capabilities, while diversifying beyond highways.
- Measured diversification into airports, railways, metro, urban infrastructure, ropeways, Wayside Amenities, PMC and technical advisory to reduce dependence on any single infrastructure segment.
- Restore sustainable profitability through disciplined execution, and improve cash flows and working-capital management - two of the five strategic pillars set out by the MD for the coming year.
- Diversify revenue streams across new infrastructure sectors and broaden the client base, including assignments funded by multilateral development institutions and financial institutions.
- Build capability for Lenders' Independent Engineer (LIE) and similar technical advisory assignments.
- Pursue international consultancy opportunities with discipline and prudence, strengthening presence across Africa and the Middle East after the first World Bank-funded assignment in Mozambique.
- Invest in technology as a differentiator - BIM and digital engineering, AI-led engineering solutions, digital twin and 3D modelling, drone and LiDAR surveying, the Infraverse digital platform and integrated ERP/analytics, under the Dhruv 2030 strategy house.
- Strengthen governance, financial discipline and internal controls - reinforced revenue recognition processes, enhanced commercial oversight, stronger project monitoring and greater accountability across project teams.
- Develop and retain technical talent, strengthen leadership capability and build a culture of continuous learning, innovation and accountability.
- Vision to 2030: be a respected, technology-driven, multidisciplinary infrastructure consultancy creating enduring value through engineering excellence, innovation and responsible growth.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Dhruv is an asset-light consultancy, so its expansion during FY 2025-26 was in verticals, geographies and capability rather than plant or capacity. The Company made a strategic entry into Airport Consultancy and a successful entry into the Wayside Amenities business, and continued expanding across Railways, Metro and Urban Infrastructure - management describes the expansion into Airports, Wayside Amenities, Railways, Metro, Urban Infrastructure and international consultancy as creating a broader and more resilient business platform. Internationally, it completed the Company's first World Bank-funded project in Mozambique and ran business development initiatives across Ghana, Saudi Arabia and the wider Middle East; a wholly owned subsidiary, Dhruv International Private Limited, was incorporated in the UK in 2024 and is still completing bank-account and other formalities, having yet to commence operations. Technology build-out continued through investment in BIM, digital engineering capabilities, technology-enabled project delivery and exploration of AI-driven engineering solutions. Order-book expansion came through new awards spanning EPC-related activities, PMC, authority engineering, DPRs and feasibility studies, construction supervision and O&M consultancy - named awards include the widening/strengthening and reconstruction to four-lane of Gola Muri in Jharkhand on EPC mode, a route alignment survey and FSR/DPR for a railway private siding for the Rohne Coal Block of NMDC, Independent Engineer services during O&M for the four-laning of the Kundapur-Surathkal section and New Mangalore Port Road Connectivity in Karnataka, PMC for the Awadh Underpass Chauraha in Lucknow, and a DPR for the ring road connecting NH-53 to NH-52 at Dhule, Maharashtra. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum is disclosed in this material.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained government capital expenditure is the primary demand driver - the Union Government has budgeted Rs. 12.22 lakh crore of capital expenditure for FY 2026-27, with effective capital expenditure estimated at Rs. 17.15 lakh crore.
- The Union Budget 2026 prioritises infrastructure, City Economic Regions, logistics networks and connectivity, which management expects to generate sustained demand for engineering consultancy, PMC, DPRs, construction supervision and technical advisory services.
- Roads and highways remain the largest addressable segment, with cumulative investments of approximately Rs. 28.5 lakh crore since FY2017 and higher NHAI/road allocations in the Union Budget 2026.
- State-level road investment momentum - particularly Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan and Odisha - is creating diversified opportunities for consultancy firms.
- Headwind flagged: National Highway project awarding has moderated due to land acquisition challenges and execution delays, though policy measures on project preparedness are expected to support execution efficiency over the medium term.
- Aviation is a new growth vector - operational airports have risen from 74 in 2014 to 165 by July 2026, and the Modified UDAN Scheme carries an outlay of Rs. 28,840 crore for FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36 to develop 100 additional airports and 200 modern helipads.
- Greenfield airport and terminal projects (Navi Mumbai, Noida/Jewar, Mopa, Kannur, Bhogapuram) are expected to raise demand for planning, design, engineering and supervision services.
- Policy programmes - PM Gati Shakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, Bharatmala Pariyojana, Sagarmala, UDAN and City Economic Regions - are reshaping the opportunity set for multidisciplinary consultants.
- Technology shift towards GIS, BIM, drone-based surveys, LiDAR mapping, intelligent transport systems and digital project monitoring favours firms with multidisciplinary technical capability.
- Competitive positioning lever: the 9th rank in India among more than 70 consultancy organisations in the latest NHAI Authority Engineer / Independent Engineer performance evaluation carries 40% weightage in upcoming AE/IE bids for NHAI and MoRTH projects.
- FY 2025-26 revenue and profitability were reduced by revisions to project cost and margin estimates under Ind AS 8 and Ind AS 115 following a review of select long-term contracts - management describes the impact as accounting in nature with no corresponding cash outflow.
- Finance cost declined on improved working capital management and lower reliance on external borrowings.
- Order Book of Rs. 224.39 Crore as on 31 March 2026 (stated in the MD's letter).
- Management states the Company continues to have a healthy order book and positive project-level profitability across most of its ongoing assignments despite the accounting-estimate revisions.
- The Directors' Report describes the order position as providing healthy revenue visibility for the coming quarters, supported by diversified mandates, long-duration contracts, sectoral expansion and a healthy order pipeline.
- Order inflow during the year comprised EPC-related activities, project management consultancy, authority engineering services, DPRs and feasibility studies, construction supervision, O&M consultancy and other allied infrastructure consultancy services; named awards include the Gola Muri four-laning EPC assignment in Jharkhand, a railway private siding FSR/DPR for the Rohne Coal Block of NMDC, Independent Engineer services for the Kundapur-Surathkal section and New Mangalore Port Road Connectivity in Karnataka, PMC for the Awadh Underpass Chauraha in Lucknow, a DPR for the Dhule city ring road connecting NH-53 to NH-52 in Maharashtra, and O&M supervision on the Hyderabad-Dindi section of NH-765 in Telangana on PBMC mode.
- HR mobilised manpower for 14 newly awarded projects during FY 2025-26, an indirect read on order inflow.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Dhruv has recovered from a temporary NHAI debarment and is accelerating growth through strategic empanelments in high-margin state and aviation infrastructure, with a clear shift from central to state-led projects and international bids in Africa and Southeast Asia, positioning it for margin expansion beyond traditional highway dependency.
